report_meta.title: Half Way Sale — Volumes, Performance & Store Execution
report_meta.subtitle: Half Way Sale Review

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Half Way Sale volumes processed grew 112.8% year-on-year to 788,798 orders, and the fulfilment funnel held up under that load — Dispatch was still up 101.8% vs LY even after the normal funnel narrowing. Service quality improved against last year during the Promo Week itself (OTD +7.9pp, Pick SLA +2.0pp), but Pick SLA fell 3.5pp below LY in the Following Week. A national shutdown disrupted courier collections over the same period, and RDO store visits flagged system downtime at 30 of the 47 stores visited.

sections.title: Volume Processed — Half Way Sale (25–30 Jun) TY vs LY
Service Performance — Promo Week vs Following Week, TY vs LY

executive_facts.statement: Volumes processed grew 112.8% year-on-year to 788,798 orders, and every downstream stage kept pace within a tight band (Picking +105.1%, Packing +103.2%, Staging +102.9%, Dispatch +101.8%) — a normal, modest funnel narrowing under materially higher load, not a sign of the operation falling behind.

Pick SLA and OTD both improved against last year during the Promo Week itself (Pick SLA +2.0pp, OTD +7.9pp), but Pick SLA fell 3.5pp behind LY in the Following Week — the strain showed up after the peak, not during it.
30 of the 47 stores visited by RDOs reported system downtime, with Western Cape (9 reports) and JHB South (6 reports) the most affected regions.

The national shutdown that disrupted courier deliveries and collections coincided directly with the Following Week's Pick SLA decline, making it the most likely single explanation for that dip rather than a broad operational failure.

Site-specific incidents — a Crown Mines power outage, generator testing, and a Silverlakes staffing gap — show the downtime problem was not purely systemic; some of it was local and preventable rather than tied to the national event.

sections.text: The Half Way Sale processed more than double last year's volume without the fulfilment funnel breaking down, but service performance softened after the promotional peak, compounded by a national shutdown and scattered site-level system and staffing incidents — the risk to manage next time is sustaining Following Week execution, not Promo Week volume.

sections.title: Store Execution — RDO Visit Consolidation (23 Jun – 2 Jul)
Root Cause Themes Reported by RDOs
sections.text:
• National shutdown / courier disruption — courier partners did not deliver, and in most cases did not collect, on the Monday/Tuesday shutdown days (raised by RDOs across Eastern Cape, Western Cape, JHB South, KZN).
  • GIF / scanner outages — scanner connectivity and image-view failures reported at multiple sites, including a national network issue causing downtime overnight.
  • Site-level power/equipment incidents — a power outage at Crown Mines halted picking/packing/staging for several hours overnight; generator testing at the same site separately cost further productive time.
  • Staffing and scheduling — Makro Silverlakes reported low productivity from absenteeism and no Acting GSM; Cape Gate had a night-shift scheduling mismatch between the correct and printed schedules.

executive_facts.statement: Reconciliation note: this consolidation's own Summary tab does not match a direct recount of the 54 visit records for three metrics (Order Drop, Dispatch Issues, Staging Issues), and two further cells (Stores Requiring Follow-up, High Priority Issues) contain broken #REF! formulas. Only Stores Visited (47) and System Downtime (30) reconcile cleanly and are reported here as hard KPIs; the other categories are described qualitatively until the source workbook is corrected.

Six of the 54 visit records have no Region recorded and two have no RDO recorded — mostly the entries describing the overnight national network/scanner outage — worth tightening the reporting template so every future entry is attributable to a region.

The Mbombela and Cornubia national network outage appears only in free-text comments, not in the structured Y/N columns, so it isn't counted in the System Downtime total above — the true downtime footprint is at least as large as reported.

provenance.extraction_notes: A third uploaded file (data__20260708T104016.894.xlsx, a raw cancelled-orders export) was excluded entirely: its date range is 6-7 July 2026, over a week after this report's period (23 June - 2 July) and after the Half Way Sale itself -- it does not describe this event and including it would misattribute unrelated data to the sale. Recommend confirming whether a cancelled-orders export covering the actual sale week exists if that detail is wanted. Separately, the Feedback Consolidation workbook's own 'Summary' tab does not reconcile against a direct recount of its 54 raw visit rows for three of its five metrics: it states 9 stores with Order Drop Issues (recount: 18), 23 with Dispatch Issues (recount: 18), and 23 with Staging Issues (recount: 19). Two further Summary cells ('Stores Requiring Follow-up', 'High Priority Issues') contain #REF! errors and could not be used at all. Only 'Total Stores Visited' (47) and 'Stores with System Downtime' (30) matched the recount exactly and are used as hard KPIs here; recommend the business correct and re-verify the Summary tab's formulas before those three other metrics are quoted in any executive-facing material.
